title: Why Do I Need to Know This
author: Science of Learning
summary: When students ask why they need to learn foundational knowledge like multiplication tables, teachers should reframe the answer toward cognitive science: foundational knowledge is valuable as a gateway concept that builds mental structures enabling future learning. New knowledge functions like a ratchet—once in long-term memory, it frees up working memory and enables increasingly complex thinking. Mathematics exemplifies this: automaticity in basic operations supports fractions, ratios, proportional reasoning, and algebra; early gaps compound into later inaccessibility.
points: Foundational knowledge teaches not because students will use it tomorrow but because it enables learning of more powerful ideas later; schools build mental structures gradually.
Automaticity in basic operations frees working memory and facilitates complex concepts; math is hierarchical and early mastery gaps snowball.
When students ask 'Why?' they often signal confusion, fatigue, or frustration; the real task is diagnosing missing prerequisite knowledge.
Understanding itself creates meaning: students who see and use growing competence stop questioning relevance; effort feels worthwhile when they experience accomplishment.
quotes: New knowledge is like a ratchet: once secured in long-term memory, it frees up working memory and enables increasingly complex thinking.

We teach multiplication tables not because adults multiply by hand, but as a gateway concept that frees working memory for fractions, ratios, proportional reasoning, and algebra.” “Learning is like constructing a multi-story building: early stages lay the foundation that supports everything that comes later.
When students ask 'Why do we need this?' they often signal confusion, fatigue, or frustration; a speech about relevance misses the point.

A student who understands is less likely to wonder why content matters; clarity, progress, and competence make effort feel worthwhile.” Archived from Science of Learning Substack on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
